text: ok now on hover highlight the grid space in the mask, then add in a few more triangles that all sit with this one, the key thing is that when hovering one triangle next to another, even if its just a sliver of grid space, it cant spill over into the touching triangle next to it
resolution: Added a hover-highlight that proves the no-spill law. The demo now renders a cluster of 6 touching triangles (a square split by both diagonals into 4, meeting at center M, plus 2 outer caps each sharing an outer edge), grid masked to their union. Wrapped the Effect in a Pressable; onMouseMove converts screen coords to surface uv (via onLayout rect) and feeds the mouse position + triangle verts into the shader as a flat data buffer. In WGSL: each fragment finds its owning triangle (argmin of IQ per-triangle signed distance) and the mouse's owning triangle; the hovered grid cell highlights a fragment ONLY if (sameCell AND fragTri==hovTri). So a cell straddling a shared edge lights just the hovered triangle's half — the neighbour's half stays dark. This is a true per-pixel geometric mask, NOT the bounding-box clamp the current Studio painter uses (which is why it leaks across slanted shared edges). Verified with a forced-hover capture on the B-M diagonal: the highlight is a triangular sliver that stops exactly at the shared edge. Builds + self-shot PASS.
